biggestGap: The three species whose identity lives in an APPENDAGE OR CONCAVITY still have none that reads — the apple has no stem well on its limb (a smooth 1.13 spheroid whose boundary cv actually FELL 0.095 -> 0.069), the strawberry has no apex and no calyx star (a crumpled red lump), and the pineapple crown is ~8 thin drooping filaments that read as a squid rather than a dense upward rosette of broad sword leaves — and the frozen probe agrees, ranking exactly those three last in BOTH pose distributions (director 2.55 / 2.90 / 2.77 against 7.73 / 10.92 / 10.18 for melon / orange / kiwi).
evidence: NO PROBE_VERSION BUMP. Everything below is PROBE_VERSION 6 as delivered; I re-derived the r5 baseline rather than quoting it, via `probes.py species src=tools/geometry-r5-snapshot.js`, and the snapshot's triangle fingerprint (3480/3144/2300/3376/5616/8376, total 26292) is exactly what I independently rebuilt in round 5, so the baseline is sound. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROUND-5 HEADLINE. I reported 'between/within = 0.91-1.18x' from a hand-rolled rasteriser. The FROZEN probe on the SAME r5 geometry reads 1.21 / 2.08 / 2.20 / 1.68 / 1.73 / 2.79 (worst 1.21, median 1.90). My r5 number was not reproducible and is withdrawn; 1.21/1.90 is the baseline of record. THE ASSIGNED QUESTION, ANSWERED YES. `probes.py species pose=so3 n=32`, r5 -> r6 separation: watermelon 2.08 -> 3.24, orange 1.21 -> 5.55, kiwi 2.20 -> 7.54, apple 1.68 -> 2.47, strawberry 1.73 -> 2.06, pineapple 2.79 -> 2.13. WORST 1.21 -> 2.06, median 1.90 -> 2.86. My round-5 fix demanded 'do not ship until the ratio clears 1.6 for EVERY species'; it clears, worst 2.06. Director pose (`species`, n=24) reproduces the builder's reported column to the digit: 7.73 / 10.92 / 10.18 / 2.55 / 2.90 / 2.77, worst 1.64 -> 2.55, median 2.08 -> 5.31. The report did not inflate a single number. TWO SPECIES ARE OUTRIGHT FIXED, and correctly, not merely differently. Orange elongation 1.221 -> 1.010, boundary cv 0.079 -> 0.008 — a true sphere, which is what a real orange's outline is; 08-citrus-caps shows a genuinely circular lower half. Kiwi 1.225 -> 1.622 with truncated poles — in 08-citrus-caps and 09/11-combo it reads as an actual kiwi, a fuzzy flat-ended barrel, and I could name it blind. Watermelon holds 1.418 -> 1.334 with a circular waist, and on the delivered frame `probes.py silhouette shots/rN/01-whole-watermelon.png` gives boundary_cv 0.1333 -> 0.0993 and max_protrusion 28.38% -> 18.13% (aspect 0.7838 -> 0.7877, mask 12139 -> 12683 px) — 01 reads as a watermelon. That is three of six nameable from outline, against zero in round 5, and it is the first round where the eye and the frozen probe agree on WHICH three. BUT THE SEPARATION GAIN IS MOSTLY DENOMINATOR, NOT NUMERATOR. For four of six species the between-species distance FELL: watermelon 0.0465 -> 0.0424, apple 0.0681 -> 0.0566, strawberry 0.0855 -> 0.0659, pineapple 0.1762 -> 0.1621. Only orange (+15%) and kiwi (+116%) actually moved away from their neighbours. What collapsed is the WITHIN-species distance, everywhere: 0.0224 -> 0.0131, 0.0240 -> 0.0060, 0.0144 -> 0.0091, 0.0405 -> 0.0229, 0.0495 -> 0.0320. The bodies became more rotationally uniform, which is a real fix for my r5 complaint ('two views of one fruit differ as much as two fruits') but is not the same thing as each body acquiring its own form — and the pineapple, the one species whose identity is pure appendage, is the ONLY one to LOSE separation, 2.79 -> 2.13, its within-distance rising 0.0632 -> 0.0761. THE EYE, ON THE DELIVERED FRAMES. Cropped 4x from 09-combo+50ms: the pineapple crown is a radial fringe of ~8 hair-thin filaments drooping away from the body, unmistakably a squid or an upside-down palm — plate-01's pineapple is ~12 broad grey-green sword leaves, each as wide as a finger and as long as the body, in a dense stiff rosette. The strawberry is a crumpled red polyhedron with no pointed apex and no sepals; the r6 header claims 'a real cone, pBot 1.34 -> 1.08' and the probe agrees the proportion moved (1.111 -> 1.246), but at ~60 px on a 640x360 buffer no cone survives. The apple is a green lump with two blown speculars and no stem, no well and no lobed base on the limb — the file spends its round on 'a 37% dish', but a polar dish only reaches the limb in the handful of poses where the polar axis is perpendicular to view, which is why its boundary cv went DOWN. WHAT THE FROZEN SUITE CANNOT SEE, SAID PLAINLY: elongation, boundary cv and the signature distance are all blind to CONCAVITY-vs-convexity and to appendage WIDTH, so 'no stem well' and 'crown leaves too thin' are not directly measurable today. I deliberately did NOT bump PROBE_VERSION for it — a v7 would invalidate four other critics' stored comparisons mid-round, and the defect is already visible indirectly in the two regressions above (pineapple separation down, apple cv down). Next round should add it on purpose. HOUSEKEEPING, ALL GOOD: star_multivalued_total 0 on both pose sets, so the cutter.js star-shaped precondition holds and no cut can produce an inverted cap; geometry cost FELL, 26292 -> 23212 tris; scene perf fell with it, peakDrawCalls 129 -> 88, peakTriangles 215606 -> 163957, cpu max 7.7 -> 3.4 ms, p95 0.5, zero errors. `void` on 01-whole-watermelon is 2.90 -> 2.93 corner max with 0.0% exact black, so the silhouette masks are not background-contaminated in either round. Hero fruit height 41.11% -> 40.56% of frame, above the 25% floor, still short of plate-01's ~55%. fix: src/fruit/geometry.js — stop authoring identity into GROSS PROPORTION, which is now done, and author it into the LIMB, which is untouched. Concretely, in the SHAPE table: (1) the pineapple crown — replace the ~8 hair filaments with 14-18 BROAD sword leaves, each at minimum 9% of the body's equatorial radius in width at its base, tapering to a point over a length of 0.9-1.2 body heights, held STIFF and swept UP at 25-40 degrees from the crown axis with only the outermost rank recurving, so the outline is a dense rosette and not a radial droop; it is the only species that lost separation (2.79 -> 2.13) and it is the most recognisable fruit in plate-01. (2) the apple — a polar dish cannot reach the limb, so move the well's signature onto the profile: give the shoulder a genuine crest whose radius exceeds the equatorial radius by 4-7%, and seat a stalk of at least 8% body radius in width and 0.35 body radii in length in the well, so 'crest -> dish -> stalk' is readable on the limb at every roll and not only at two poles. (3) the strawberry — its apex curvature radius must be <= 6% of the equatorial radius and the calyx must show 5 distinct sepal tips standing PROUD of the shoulder by >= 12% of body radius, so the k<=3 profile alone draws a heart. Then add a `limb` probe to tools/probes.py (bumping to PROBE_VERSION 7 deliberately, at the start of the round, not the end): over the same SO(3) pose set, report per species the angular fraction of the boundary that is CONCAVE beyond 2% of mean radius, and the median angular WIDTH of every convex protrusion above a k<=3 fit. Do not ship until apple concave fraction >= 6%, strawberry >= 8% with five protrusions, and pineapple median protrusion width >= 6 degrees; all three are near zero today.
